items.title: Brent eased to USD 104.37 on Friday - down 2% on the day, still up 1% on the week
items.summary: Brent settled at USD 104.37 on Friday 25 September, down 2.09% in a day, but still more than 1% higher across the week and 50.8% above the same week last year. The pullback came on peace-talk headlines, not on supply: export flows through Hormuz reached 33.7 million barrels this week, roughly on a par with the week before. The premium has stopped rising, but it has not come off.
items.source: TradingEconomics Brent CFD, settle 2026-09-25 (104.37, -2.09%; monthly +20.05%, yearly +50.78%); straits.live Hormuz dashboard 2026-09-25 2158Z (Brent 104.37, market closed; 7-day flow 33.7m bbl)

items.title: The seven-day timetable is now on paper - a phased US-Iran deal to reopen Hormuz
items.summary: Iran has given Washington a seven-day sequence: on day six the Strait of Hormuz reopens along a route designated by Oman and Iran, and nuclear talks start the following day. The conditions attached are the old June memorandum of understanding - unfreeze Iranian assets, allow oil exports, end the war on all fronts, lift the naval blockade - but the speed is new. US and Iranian negotiators are reported to be exploring the phased structure; Tehran says it is still waiting for Trump's answer.
items.source: The Guardian 2026-09-25 (Wintour; day-by-day timetable); Bloomberg 2026-09-24 'US, Iran to Explore Phased Deal to Reopen Hormuz'; Reuters/US News 2026-09-24; CNBC 2026-09-25 (Iran offer, seven days, conditions)

items.title: Hormuz still closed on the water - the offer gained detail, not compliance
items.summary: The strait remains shut to commercial shipping, now on day 209 since the closure was declared, and the live tracker puts the binding constraint on war-risk insurance rather than on any blockade. IMF PortWatch's latest published day (20 September) shows one commercial transit against a typical 85 per day - about 1% of pre-crisis volume - and the reopen-by-30-September odds are quoted at 1%. A signed seven-day plan and a re-opened strait are two different facts; only the first exists.
items.source: straits.live 2026-09-25 2158Z (Day 209, status: closed to commercial shipping by war-risk insurance; PortWatch 2026-09-20: 1 transit vs 85/day; reopening odds 1% by 30 Sep; crisis pressure 89/100)

items.title: PETRONAS and Sarawak each want their petition heard first - the court will decide the sequence
items.summary: At the summons for direction on 24 September, PETRONAS argued its petition should go first because it was filed first (10 January, leave granted 16 March). The Sarawak government wants its own petition (filed 23 February) heard first and wants a preliminary issue decided - the colonial-era Sarawak (Alteration of Boundaries) Order in Council 1954, which fixes the Sarawak-Sabah border. The two challenges are directed at different statutes: PETRONAS challenges Sarawak state law, Sarawak challenges federal law. Consolidated or separate is the open question.
items.source: The Star 2026-09-24; Borneo Post 2026-09-24 (Justice Rhodzariah Bujang, summons for direction; Cyrus Das for PETRONAS)

items.title: Budget 2027 lands on 9 October - 13 days out, and the arithmetic has changed under it
items.summary: The Ministry of Finance has confirmed 9 October 2026 for tabling, the fifth MADANI budget and the second under the Thirteenth Plan. The pre-budget statement (18 August) names three priorities - raise the ceiling, raise the floor, drive reform - and explicitly frames 2026 as the year crude went above USD 100 and the country held. What it does not yet name is the oil-price assumption the numbers are built on. The 2026 budget assumed USD 65; the market is at USD 104.
items.source: Ministry of Finance, Pre-Budget Statement 2027, 2026-08-18 (tabled 9 October 2026); Star 2026-07-23

items.title: Every USD 1 on Brent is worth about RM 300 million - and the 2027 forecasts point the other way
items.summary: Government-linked analysis puts each USD 1 per barrel rise in crude at roughly RM 300 million of additional petroleum-related revenue, through PETRONAS dividends and petroleum income tax. But the near-term revenue assumption was set low: PETRONAS' RM 20 billion dividend for 2026 was negotiated against an assumption of about USD 60-65. Against that, the forward forecasts are bearish - the IEA sees 2027 supply growth of about 8 million barrels per day against demand growth of about 2 million, and JP Morgan has published a USD 30s scenario for 2027. Budget 2027 has to pick a number between a hot spot market and a glut forecast.
items.source: Sinar Daily (RM 300m per USD 1); 27 Advisory (PETRONAS RM 20bn 2026 dividend negotiated at USD 60-65); IEA 2027 outlook as reported; JP Morgan 2027 USD 30s scenario

items.title: RM 1.8 billion of offshore installation work awarded - Carigali and PTTEP, execution into 2027
items.summary: Vantris Energy secured two transportation and installation work orders worth a combined RM 1.8 billion (about USD 441.8 million) from PETRONAS Carigali and PTTEP subsidiaries for offshore work in Malaysian waters. Execution starts in the quarter ending 31 January 2027 and is scheduled to finish in the quarter ending 31 January 2028. It is a real capex signal: work booked now, spread across exactly the period OD1 sits in.
items.source: The Star 2026-09-25; Bursa announcement via Offshore Energy / IndexBox 2026-09-25 (RM 1.8bn; USD 441.8m; FY ending 31 Jan 2027 Q3 to FY ending 31 Jan 2028 Q4)

items.title: A new LNG carrier joins the PETRONAS fleet - Puteri Kelantan, delivered 24 September
items.summary: Puteri Kelantan, an LNG carrier built for Petronas LNG, was delivered on 24 September 2026 at Hudong-Zhonghua in China. It sits alongside the 14 September METLEN supply agreement for Southeast Europe as the LNG portfolio continues to widen away from the traditional Asian buyer base. Neither is a demand move; both are logistics capacity committed years ahead.
items.source: Cyprus Shipping News 2026-09-25 (Kawasaki Kisen Kaisha; delivery 2026-09-24, Hudong-Zhonghua); PETRONAS media release 2026-09-14 (METLEN LNG supply agreement)

items.title: OPS: one yellow - WELL is reporting a self-report, not a sensor
items.summary: arifOS, FED, A-FORGE, GEOX, FLOW, FRAME and HERMES all answer healthy. WELL answers degraded: its last human signal is 46.3 hours old and its own honesty block labels the source OPERATOR_REPORTED / SELF_REPORT, not wearable telemetry. Nothing is broken; one yellow is the machine saying it cannot see the body it is meant to watch.

items.title: WALL MOVED: 1 October fixes the sequence; the substantive window is still late January 2027
items.summary: The court fixed Thursday 1 October for the next summons for direction - the day the order of the two petitions and Sarawak's preliminary objection get settled. The one-week substantive hearing itself remains provisionally late January 2027, which puts it inside both the Sarawak campaign season and the OD1 window. Until 1 October this is a date, not a decision.
items.source: The Star 2026-09-24 (Justice Rhodzariah fixed next Thursday - 1 October 2026 - for further summons for direction)

items.title: WALL: Bintulu LNG jurisdiction still contested - no filing has moved it this week
items.summary: The question of which regulator governs the Bintulu LNG complex remains unresolved, and nothing published this week advances it. It stays recorded as contested rather than retired: silence from the parties is not a resolution, and PETRONAS' revenue exposure to Sarawak gas sits behind it. Kept on the wall so a quiet week cannot read as a closed one.
items.source: carried from EDITION-010 (no new filing found in searches 2026-09-25/26); see petronas-pda-petition-scope for the live litigation calendar

items.title: WALL UNRESOLVED: the oil-price assumption inside Budget 2027 has not been published
items.summary: The pre-budget statement of 18 August sets priorities, not numbers, and no official table yet states the crude assumption Budget 2027 is built on. This is UNRESOLVED in the strict sense - knowable, and due to be known on 9 October - not WITHDRAWN. Until it is published, every projection of subsidy cost and petroleum revenue is arithmetic on an assumed price, and should be read as such.
items.source: MOF Pre-Budget Statement 2027, 2026-08-18 (no crude assumption stated); Budget 2026 baseline of USD 65 per barrel as reported by New Straits Times 2026-09-10

items.title: War-risk cover now prices a Hormuz passage at about USD 10 million for a supertanker
items.summary: Insurance, not navies, is what keeps the strait shut. Tanker war-risk cover is being quoted at roughly 40 times the pre-crisis rate - around USD 10 million for one VLCC round the passage - with six protection and indemnity clubs withdrawn from the trade. It is the slowest variable in the whole chain: even after a political deal is signed, cover has to be re-priced and re-underwritten before hulls move. That lag is why a headline deal and a restored flow are not the same date.
items.source: straits.live 2026-09-25 2158Z (war-risk VLCC approx. USD 10.0M; 40.0x pre-crisis; six P&I clubs withdrawn; insurance reading last set 17 days ago vs transits 5 days ago)

items.title: Nobody told you the way car loans are priced changed in June
items.summary: From 1 June 2026 the Hire-Purchase (Amendment) Act abolished both the flat rate and the Rule of 78, and requires loans to be quoted on the effective interest rate and a reducing balance. The practical effect is that early settlement stops being penalised - the old method front-loaded interest so that paying a loan off early cost you more than the maths allowed. If there is a vehicle loan in the household taken before June, the settlement figure quoted under the old formula is now the wrong number. Ask for the EIR and the reducing-balance statement.
items.source: Hire Purchase (Term Charges) Regulations 2026 [P.U.(A) 171/2026] in force 1 June 2026; Hire-Purchase (Amendment) Act 2026; reporting via paultan.org 2025-11-14, iMoney 2026, Baker McKenzie alert, RinggitPlus

items.title: Still open: check the EPF nomination once before OD1
items.summary: A nomination is voided by marriage, divorce or a change of marital status, and the fund does not write to tell you. It is a five-minute check that removes a slow-moving liability from the middle of an exit year. Carried forward unchanged; no new information this week.
items.source: carried from EDITION-010; EPF nomination rules (EPF Act 1991)

items.title: Still open: AI-generated intimate images already fall inside the criminal definition
items.summary: Carried forward unchanged. The point recorded previously - that synthetically generated intimate imagery of a real person is not outside the law merely because no camera was involved - still stands, and no new instrument has changed it this week. Retained because the people who need to know this are usually told the opposite.
items.source: carried from EDITION-010 (no repeal or amendment found in searches 2026-09-25/26)

items.title: A form of boron that shouldn't exist: it bends, and it conducts
items.summary: Chemists made a boron allotrope, Imma-B60, that is both electrically conductive and plastically deformable, a combination that had lived on paper for over a decade. The route: form a Na4B60 precursor under high pressure, then drive the sodium out. The reporting disagrees on how much better it conducts - Nature news says a million times more than chemists expected, phys.org says ten million - so treat the exact factor as unsettled and the direction as solid. Boron is famously stiff and insulating; this one is neither.
items.source: Nature Chemistry 2026 (10.1038/s41557-026-02267-7, 'An open-framework boron allotrope exhibiting high conductivity and plasticity'); Nature news 2026-09-23/24 (a million times more conductive); phys.org 2026-09 (ten million); figures disagree between origins - recorded, not reconciled

items.title: Tonight and tomorrow: the Harvest Moon comes up beside Saturn
items.summary: The full moon of 26-27 September is the Harvest Moon, and it rises in close approach to Saturn, which is bright now ahead of its opposition on 4 October. From Kedah the pair clears the horizon in the evening; the moon will look round and bright on both nights. No equipment needed - it is the one night sky event this year that shows up through haze.
items.source: timeanddate.com 'Moon Guide for September 2026' (26 September: Harvest Moon and Saturn close approach; Saturn opposition 4 October); Travel And Tour World 2026-09 (Malaysia, 26-27 September)

items.title: Two snail species nobody had named, found in Montenegro
items.summary: Researchers described two new tiny snail species from Montenegro - a reminder that Europe still contains small animals unknown to science. The finding matters less for the snails than for the method: the species were separated by shell and genital anatomy under a microscope, the classical way, not by genetic sequencing alone. Careful looking still produces new species.
items.source: ScienceDaily 2026-09-24 (two new tiny snail species, Montenegro)

items.title: Pump band for 24-30 September: BUDI95 held at RM 1.99, the open-market price up another 20 sen
items.summary: For the week of 24-30 September, RON95 under BUDI95 is unchanged at RM 1.99 a litre. Everything not subsidised moved up again: unsubsidised RON95 RM 4.57 (+20 sen), RON97 RM 5.05 (+20 sen), diesel RM 5.42 (+15 sen) in the Peninsula. The next band is announced Wednesday 30 September and takes effect Thursday 1 October. The gap between RM 1.99 and RM 4.57 is the size of the decision Budget 2027 has to make.
items.source: Ministry of Finance weekly APM prices via paultan.org fuel-price tracker, data refreshed 2026-09-24, week of 24-30 September 2026; data.gov.my fuelprice dataset

items.title: The subsidy bill: about RM 40 billion at these prices, against RM 49 billion budgeted for everything
items.summary: The Prime Minister said in July that petrol and diesel subsidies could reach close to RM 40 billion in 2026 if prices persist - more than double the original estimate - with the monthly bill rising roughly tenfold to around RM 7 billion. Budget 2026 allocated RM 49 billion for subsidies and social assistance in total, and was built on USD 65 crude. HSBC has said Malaysia may need to adjust the RON95 subsidy to stay on its 2026 deficit target. The pressure lands on 9 October, and it can only be released three ways: higher deficit, higher pump prices, or a quota cut.
items.source: PM Anwar, 2026-07-01 (Bloomberg, Malay Mail: RM 40bn; USD 9.8bn); The Edge / HSBC Global Investment Research (monthly bill RM 7bn; RON95 review); New Straits Times 2026-09-10 (Budget 2026 RM 49bn subsidies, USD 65 assumption)

items.title: Haze: four Sarawak stations unhealthy; Kedah still clear
items.summary: As of 9am on 25 September four Sarawak areas were unhealthy - Serian 178, Kuching 166, Samarahan 165, Sri Aman 163 - with Serian's reading at the district police headquarters. No active warning covers Kuala Muda or the rest of Kedah, and Sungai Petani's last unhealthy reading recorded here was 155 on 17 September. The trigger to watch is the school-closure threshold at API 200 and the emergency declaration above 300; neither has been reached.
items.source: BERNAMA 2026-09-25 (Serian 178, Kuching 166, Samarahan 165, Sri Aman 163); Malay Mail 2026-09-25 and 2026-09-17 (Sungai Petani 155); DOE APIMS / MyEQMS portal

items.title: Still open: 97 days until the household electricity threshold drops back to 600 kWh
items.summary: The raised protection band of 800 kWh runs only for September to December 2026; it reverts to 600 kWh on 1 January 2027. At the boundary the AFA adjustment, the RM 10 retail charge waiver and the 8% service tax exemption all switch off together, so the step at 601 kWh is large relative to one extra unit. Carried forward unchanged - the date is fixed and nothing has changed it.
items.source: MOF/TNB announcement 2026-09-17 as reported by paultan.org; TNB tariff schedule 1 July 2025 - 31 December 2027

items.title: Still open: coal at USD 148 a tonne is the input the shield is currently absorbing
items.summary: The generation-cost input behind the electricity tariff sits well above the level that would normally pass through to bills, and the current protection is what keeps it off households. Carried forward unchanged; no new generation-cost data point this week. It is the reason the January threshold revert is a fiscal decision rather than a technical one.
items.source: carried from EDITION-010; no update found 2026-09-25/26

items.title: OD1: 162 days - and the two live legal calendars both now fall inside it
items.summary: From today, 162 days to 7 March 2027. The Federal Court sequence is decided on 1 October and the substantive hearing sits provisionally in late January 2027, which is inside the window and inside the Sarawak campaign season. Budget 2027 lands 9 October, 13 days out, carrying the USD 65 assumption against a USD 104 market. None of these force a decision today; all three are dates that will be spent whether or not anything is decided.
items.source: computed 2026-09-26 (OD1 2027-03-07 = 162 days; FC sequence 1 Oct = 5 days; budget 9 Oct = 13 days; provisional hearing 25 Jan 2027 = 121 days); FC date per The Star 2026-09-24; budget date per MOF

items.title: Still open: the substantive hearing sits inside Sarawak's campaign season
items.summary: The provisional late-January 2027 hearing window overlaps the period in which Sarawak is expected to be in election mode, and the state government's own petition keeps it live. No new date published this week. Kept on the wall as a clock, not a commentary: it is a constraint on when the PDA 1974 question can be answered, not a statement about who wins anything.
items.source: carried from EDITION-010; sequence date 1 October 2026 per The Star 2026-09-24; Sarawak assembly dissolution timeline per published state-election reporting
